correctness.rationale: Linear change to same-parity lattice converts the diamond to two intervals; each interval has n or n+1 points per parity, and joint parity alignment is measured by two disjoint torus diamonds of area 2s² (or 2t²). Separate all cases and verify probability total 1 and mean 2R². The two interval increment indicators are independent by Haar invariance; bounded parity remainder gives the centered binomial limit. Rational checker independently tests finite cases; no infinite claim rests on sampling.

originality.rationale: The exact mean is classical and the variance is covered by Rosen 1989 and Holgate 1990. Their literature does not state the four-atom *complete* PMF for the shifted 45-degree diamond or the two-Bernoulli phase limit. Schlie 2026 poses broad distribution questions; de Bruijn 1965 considers a different randomly oriented thin-rectangle model. Equivalent methods and broad coverage were compared; Rosen full PDF remained inaccessible, and undiscovered historical tables are residual risks.

value.rationale: A complete distribution of a natural fixed-rational-angle randomly translated convex-body lattice count, not merely a variance or numerical table; the finite four-atom support and exact phase-dependent centered binomial law expose a rigid arithmetic lattice-symmetry phenomenon, including exceptional degenerate phases with residual unscaled randomness. This is an explicitly scoped benchmark for random lattice discretization, not a claimed extension to arbitrary shapes.
